department: Centre for Infrastructural Monitoring and Protection
summary: Two ARC-funded PhD scholarships to develop a city-scale framework for monitoring ageing bridges using drive-by sensing data from crowdsourced moving vehicles, combining physics-informed AI, signal processing and modal identification.
title: Structural health monitoring by using generative and physics-informed AI

department: Centre for Infrastructural Monitoring and Protection
summary: PhD scholarships in the Centre for Infrastructural Monitoring and Protection covering a three-year stipend and tuition fees, for research in structural dynamics, earthquake engineering, structural health monitoring, concrete materials and blast and impact engineering; positions open until filled.
title: PhD student scholarships – Civil and Structural Engineering

department: School of Civil Engineering and Construction
summary: ARC-funded PhD scholarship under Prof. Alex (Ching-Tai) Ng investigating non-contact ultrasonic wave generation, propagation and measurement for damage detection in structures with challenging surface conditions; full scholarship covering tuition fees and a living allowance, open until filled.
title: Non-contact Ultrasonic Techniques for Damage Detection in Structures with Challenging Surface Conditions

department: School of Civil Engineering and Construction
summary: PhD scholarship under Prof. Alex (Ching-Tai) Ng to develop an advanced non-contact ultrasonic inspection system for structural safety inspection, using structural health monitoring and nondestructive evaluation techniques; full scholarship covering tuition fees and a living allowance, open until filled.
title: Development of an Advanced Non-contact Ultrasonic Inspection System for Structural Safety Inspection

department: School of Civil and Environmental Engineering
summary: PhD positions on a CRC-P project with Pells Consulting and Sunwater developing robotic and automated tools to model erosion of dam spillways, covering UAV/USV surveys, rock-mass and CFD modelling of scour, and physical hydraulic modelling.
title: Smart Tech for Safer Dams: Tackling Erosion with Innovation – PhD positions

department: Department of Civil, Environmental and Mining Engineering
summary: PhD scholarship in the Australian Centre for Geomechanics for graduates in civil or mining engineering to research evidence-based approaches to geotechnical stability and risk minimisation for tailings facilities.
title: PhD Scholarship in Geotechnical Engineering: Evidence based approaches to ensuring geotechnical stability and minimising risks associated with tailings facilities

summary: Open PhD project repurposing decommissioned subsea flowlines into dynamically installed anchors for floating wind, wave and solar devices, using hydrodynamic and geotechnical numerical analysis plus centrifuge and field testing; requires a master's in geotechnical, structural or mechanical engineering.
title: Repurposing decommissioned oil and gas flowlines to dynamically installed anchors for harnessing marine renewable energies and removing ocean plastics

summary: PhD scholarship on residual strength degradation and fatigue behaviour of composite laminates for damage tolerance design of critical aerospace structures, developing methods to characterise hybrid, multifunctional braided and fibre metal laminate composites.
title: PhD Scholarship in Damage Tolerant Hybrid Composite Materials for Applications in Critical Aerospace Structures
